lessonTitle: Concept Generation: Function Structures and Morphological Charts

blocks.text: A village cooperative wants a hand-operated grain mill for use without electricity. The first idea a team shouts out is a hand crank turning two stones. Twenty minutes later nobody has asked what the mill actually has to do, and the team has one concept, not a choice.

blocks.markdown: Good design compares **several** genuinely different concepts before committing to one. Two tools make that systematic. A **function structure** says what the product must do, in terms of flows entering and leaving, without saying how. A **morphological chart** then lists ways of achieving each sub-function and lets you combine them.

blocks.title: Function structure
blocks.text: A function structure is a diagram of the overall function of a product, broken into sub-functions linked by the three kinds of flow: **energy**, **material** and **signal (information)**. Each sub-function is written as a verb plus a noun (for example, convert energy, crush grain) and contains no component names. The overall function is a black box with its inputs on the left and outputs on the right.

blocks.markdown: Decomposition proceeds top-down: draw the overall function as one box, then split it into the smaller transformations that must occur between inputs and outputs, until each sub-function is simple enough that you can think of several ways to do it. Writing functions without naming parts keeps you from fixating on the first solution.

blocks.title: Function structure for a hand-operated grain mill
blocks.prompt: Produce a function structure for a hand-operated grain mill. Inputs: grain, human effort. Outputs: flour, husk (waste).

steps.text: State the overall function as a black box: it converts whole grain and human energy into flour and waste.

List the transformations in order. Energy path: import human energy, convert it to rotation, transmit and change the speed of rotation. Material path: store and feed grain, crush grain, separate flour from husk, collect flour.

Check that every sub-function is a verb plus a noun and that none names a part (a gearbox or a stone would be a solution, not a function), and that every flow in the overall function appears as an input or output of some sub-function.

The grinding sub-function links the two paths: it takes grain and rotational energy and delivers crushed material. The result is a connected set of boxes that no particular concept has yet been chosen to satisfy.

blocks.answer: Sub-functions: import energy, convert to rotation, transmit rotation, feed grain, crush grain, separate husk, collect flour. Flows: energy, material (grain, flour, husk).

blocks.markdown: The **morphological chart** places the sub-functions as rows and lists solution principles, or means, for each in columns. Any path through the chart that picks one means per row is a candidate concept. If the rows have $n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k$ options, the number of possible combinations is the product.

blocks.caption: Total number of combinations in a morphological chart with k sub-functions and n_i options each.
Fragment of a chart for the grain mill (blank cell: only two options).

blocks.title: Counting combinations and forming concepts
blocks.prompt: For the chart above, how many combinations exist, and write down three distinct concepts.

steps.text: Concept A: hand crank, direct drive, stone discs, gravity hopper (a simple traditional quern). Concept B: foot pedal, belt and pulley, steel burr plates, gravity hopper (hands-free, faster). Concept C: hand lever, spur gear train, hammer beater, hand scoop (percussive crushing).
These three differ in how energy is provided and how grain is crushed, which are the main principles of the product, so they are different ideas rather than small variations of one idea.

blocks.answer: 54 combinations; A, B and C are three distinct concepts. Not all combinations are feasible, so incompatible ones are removed first.

blocks.markdown: **Combining sub-solutions.** Pick a path through the chart for each concept, favouring combinations that use different means for the most important sub-functions. At least three genuinely different concepts should be carried forward to selection, because comparing a single option or near-copies of one gives no real choice. Remove combinations that cannot work (for example a foot pedal for a design that must be carried on a bicycle rack) and record why.

items: Write functions as verb plus noun, with no component names.
Show energy, material and signal flows separately.
Fill every row with several means before combining, including unusual ones.
Build concepts that differ in principle, not just in dimensions or rating.
Screen for compatibility and note the reason for every rejected combination.

blocks.title: Parameter variants are not concepts
blocks.text: A 12 V motor and a 24 V motor driving the same gearbox are the same concept with different sizing. If three concepts differ only in numerical parameters, the selection stage compares nothing of substance and the design may miss a better solution.

blocks.title: Function first, solution second
blocks.text: Define what must happen (function structure) before listing how it can happen (morphological chart). Then combine different means into at least three distinct concepts before selecting among them.

points: A function structure decomposes the overall function into verb-noun sub-functions linked by energy, material and signal flows, naming no components.
A morphological chart lists means for each sub-function; the number of combinations is the product of the numbers of options in the rows.
At least three concepts that differ in principle, not in parameters, are formed from compatible combinations and carried forward to selection.

questions.stem: Which entry is correctly written as a sub-function in a function structure?

options.text: Use a 12 V brushed DC motor

distractorRationale.b: Names a particular component, which is a solution rather than a function.
distractorRationale.c: Names a part and a step of assembly, not a function.
distractorRationale.d: Describes qualities of the product, which belong in the requirements, not the function structure.

questions.explanation: A sub-function is a verb plus a noun that describes a transformation of a flow, independent of the means. Naming a motor or gearbox already commits to a solution and defeats the purpose of the decomposition.

questions.stem: In a function structure, which three kinds of flow are traditionally shown?

options.text: Input, process and feedback loop only

distractorRationale.b: These are quantities in mechanics, not flow types in a function structure.
distractorRationale.d: This lists parts of a block diagram, not the three types of flow.

questions.explanation: A function structure tracks what enters and leaves each sub-function as energy, material (including matter that is processed) or signal (information). Distinguishing them helps spot missing sub-functions such as sensing or waste removal.

questions.stem: What does a morphological chart contain?

options.text: Rows of sub-functions, each with a list of alternative means of achieving it
A weighted comparison of finished designs against criteria
A schedule of tasks over time
A list of tolerances for each dimension

questions.correctOptionText: Rows of sub-functions, each with a list of alternative means of achieving it

distractorRationale.b: This describes a weighted decision matrix used after concepts exist.
distractorRationale.d: This describes a drawing or tolerance schedule.

questions.explanation: The chart is a generation tool: each row is a sub-function and the columns hold different means. A concept is formed by choosing one means per row.

questions.stem: A team proposes three concepts for a portable water filter: all use the same hand pump and membrane, and differ only in whether the casing is 50 mm, 60 mm or 70 mm in diameter. What is the main problem?

options.text: The concepts differ only in a parameter, so the team has effectively one concept
Three concepts are too many to compare
The casing diameter has no effect on a hand-pumped filter
Concepts should never be compared before the detail design stage

questions.correctOptionText: The concepts differ only in a parameter, so the team has effectively one concept

distractorRationale.b: At least three are wanted; the issue is that they are not different.
distractorRationale.c: Diameter might matter, but that is not the issue here.
distractorRationale.d: Concept comparison happens before detail design, not after.

questions.explanation: Concepts must differ in principle, such as the pumping means, the filtration principle or the energy source. Changing a diameter is sizing within a single concept and gives no real choice at selection.

questions.stem: A function structure for a coffee machine should specify the make and model of the heating element for the sub-function 'heat water'.
questions.explanation: The function structure describes what must be done, and naming a heating element already picks a solution. Alternatives for heating, such as thermoblock, kettle element or induction, are generated later in the morphological chart.

questions.stem: A morphological chart for a seed-planting device has four sub-functions with 4, 3, 5 and 2 means respectively. How many distinct combinations does the chart contain?
questions.explanation: The number of combinations is the product $4\times3\times5\times2=120$. Each combination is a candidate concept before incompatible pairs are removed.

questions.stem: A chart for a window-cleaning robot has sub-functions with 3, 3, 4 and 2 means (72 combinations). Option 3 of the first sub-function is incompatible with options 1 and 2 of the second sub-function, and is compatible with everything else. How many combinations remain feasible?
questions.explanation: The total is $3\times3\times4\times2=72$. Combinations containing first-row option 3 together with second-row option 1 or 2 number $1\times2\times4\times2=16$, so $72-16=56$ remain feasible. Screening for compatibility reduces the field before concepts are chosen.

questions.stem: A portable tyre inflator takes electrical energy from a 12 V vehicle socket and delivers air at a controlled pressure to a tyre valve. Produce a function structure for it: list the overall inputs and outputs and at least five sub-functions, identifying the type of flow between them.
markingGuide: Overall inputs: electrical energy, ambient air, user setting (signal); outputs: pressurised air, heat or noise (waste), pressure reading
Sub-functions written as verb plus noun, such as import electrical energy, convert electrical energy to motion, compress air, measure pressure, stop at set pressure, deliver air to valve
Energy flow, material (air) flow and signal flow (pressure sensing and shut-off) identified separately
No components named in the sub-functions
Flows are connected logically from inputs to outputs
questions.explanation: A complete answer separates energy, air (material) and pressure information (signal), and writes each sub-function as a transformation rather than a component. Including measure and shut-off shows that the signal flow was considered.

questions.stem: For a device that cleans the outside of windows on a tall building, build a small morphological chart with three sub-functions and at least three means each, then combine them into three distinct concepts. State how many combinations the chart contains and justify why your three concepts are distinct.
markingGuide: Three sub-functions written as functions, such as move across surface, apply cleaning, remove dirt or water
At least three different means in each row
Correct count by multiplication of the options per row
Three concepts, each a choice of one means per row, with different principles for at least the main sub-function
Justification that the concepts differ in principle, not only in size or rating
questions.explanation: A good chart lists real alternatives and the total count is the product of row counts. The concepts are distinct when they differ in the underlying principle (for example suction, cable-hung or drone-based motion) rather than in sizing.

questions.stem: A team has a chart for a grain-sorting machine and proposes: Concept 1, a 12 V motor with spur gears; Concept 2, a 12 V motor with helical gears; Concept 3, a 24 V motor with spur gears. All other means are identical. Evaluate these as concepts and suggest how to improve the set.
markingGuide: Identifies that all three share the same principle and differ only in sizing or minor detail
Explains that the selection stage would then compare little of substance
Recognises that distinct concepts should differ in the means of the key sub-functions (for example sorting by size, colour or weight)
Suggests using other rows of the chart to build different combinations
Notes that incompatibilities should still be screened
questions.explanation: The set offers no real alternatives, so the best solution may never be examined. Concepts should vary the means in the principal sub-functions, as shown in the chart, and then be screened for compatibility.
